answer=1 raw='<think>The question asks about which method ensures proper triangulation of concave surfaces so that no area outside the computational domain is triangulated.

Advancing front method - This method builds the mesh from the boundary inward, which naturally respects the boundary shape and concave regions. It triangulates only inside the domain defined by the front.

Bowyer-Watson algorithm - This is a Delaunay-based method. It can create triangles outside the domain if not properly constrained, especially in concave regions where the Delaunay triangulation may not respect the boundary.

The advancing front method is specifically designed to handle complex boundaries and concave surfaces properly because it constructs the mesh based on the boundary definition.

So the answer is 1 - Advancing front method.</think>
